  - title: 'Forget the F-22 or F-35: China’s Stealth Fighters Might Soon Be Invisible
      to Space-Based Radar'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/forger-the-f-22-or-f-35-chinas-stealth-fighters-might-soon-be-invisible-to-space-based-radar/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Chinese researchers linked to CASIC report a microwave-absorbing
      aircraft coating for stealth fighters and bombers that is derived from dried loofah
      and aims to reduce detection by space-based radar. -The process carbonizes loofah
      into a porous carbon network and embeds nickel-cobalt oxide (NiCo₂O₄) nanoparticles,
      producing an NCO-2 composite layer about […] The post Forget the F-22 or F-35:
      China’s Stealth Fighters Might Soon Be Invisible to Space-Based Radar appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Chinese researchers have developed a microwave-absorbing aircraft
      coating made from carbonized loofah and embedded nickel-cobalt oxide nanoparticles,
      which aims to enhance the stealth capabilities of fighters and bombers against
      space-based radar detection.
    paragraph_summary: Chinese researchers from the China Aerospace Science and Industry
      Corporation (CASIC) have developed a microwave-absorbing coating for stealth aircraft,
      including fighters and bombers, derived from dried loofah. This innovative coating
      aims to enhance stealth capabilities by reducing detection by space-based radar.
      The process involves carbonizing loofah to create a porous carbon network, which
      is then infused with nickel-cobalt oxide (NiCo₂O₄) nanoparticles, resulting in
      a composite layer known as NCO-2. This advancement could potentially make China's
      stealth fighters less detectable compared to existing models like the F-22 and
      F-35.
    published: '2025-12-18T12:28:45+00:00'

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-u-s-military-can-take-back-the-medal-of-honor/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The Medal of Honor is America’s highest military

      first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The article discusses how the Medal of Honor, the highest
      military decoration in the U.S., can be revoked, highlighting cases such as Dr.
      Mary Walker and the 27th Maine, and examining the reasons behind the revocation
      of hundreds of medals throughout history.
    paragraph_summary: The Medal of Honor, the highest military decoration in the United
      States, can be revoked under certain circumstances, as explored by expert Christian
      D. Orr. The article highlights the history of this revocation process, detailing
      cases such as that of Dr. Mary Walker, a Civil War surgeon who lost her medal
      for decades, and the 27th Maine regiment, which received medals collectively.
      The discussion emphasizes that while the Medal of Honor is a prestigious accolade,
      it is not necessarily a permanent recognition, reflecting the evolving standards
      and accountability within the military.

  - title: U.S. Army and U.S. Navy Miscalculated Number of Low-Scoring Recruits Entering
      U.S. Military, IG Finds
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/u-s-army-and-u-s-navy-miscalculated-number-of-low-scoring-recruits-entering-u-s-military-ig-finds/
    text: Key Points and Summary – A Pentagon Inspector General review found the Army
      and Navy miscalculated Category IV enlistments—AFQT scores in the 10th–30th percentile—by
      using improved prep-course scores instead of initial results. -That approach let
      both services exceed the 4% statutory cap without required Secretary approval
      and congressional notification. -The Navy also ran a pilot […] The post U.S. Army
      and U.S. Navy Miscalculated Number of Low-Scoring Recruits Entering U.S. Military,
      IG Finds appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: A Pentagon Inspector General review revealed that the Army
      and Navy miscalculated the number of low-scoring recruits by using improved prep-course
      scores instead of initial AFQT results, allowing them to exceed the 4% statutory
      cap without necessary approvals.
    paragraph_summary: A Pentagon Inspector General review revealed that the Army and
      Navy miscalculated their enlistments of Category IV recruits—those with Armed
      Forces Qualification Test (AFQT) scores in the 10th to 30th percentile—by relying
      on improved scores from prep courses rather than initial test results. This miscalculation
      allowed both branches to exceed the 4% statutory cap on low-scoring recruits without
      obtaining the necessary approval from the Secretary of Defense or notifying Congress.
      Additionally, the Navy conducted a pilot program related to this issue.
    published: '2025-12-17T23:52:07+00:00'

  - title: The U.S. Military’s On Again, Off Again War on Shaving
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-u-s-militarys-on-again-off-again-war-on-shaving/
    text: Key Points and Summary – Military beards were common in the Civil War, but
      World War I gas-mask requirements made clean-shaven faces the norm. -The Navy
      briefly reversed course in 1970 under Adm. Elmo Zumwalt, then reinstated the ban
      in 1984. -After 9/11, some special operators grew beards overseas, while religious
      and medical waivers expanded […] The post The U.S. Military’s On Again, Off Again
      War on Shaving appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. military's stance on beards has fluctuated over time,
      from their prevalence during the Civil War to a clean-shaven requirement during
      World War I, a brief allowance in the Navy in the 1970s, and a resurgence of beards
      among special operators post-9/11, reflecting ongoing debates about grooming standards.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the fluctuating policies regarding facial
      hair in the U.S. military, highlighting that while beards were common during the
      Civil War, World War I's gas-mask requirements led to a clean-shaven standard.
      In 1970, under Adm. Elmo Zumwalt, the Navy briefly allowed beards, but this was
      reversed in 1984. Following the events of 9/11, some special operators began growing
      beards in overseas deployments, and the military has since expanded religious
      and medical waivers regarding shaving, reflecting an ongoing debate about grooming
      standards.
    published: '2025-12-17T23:26:10+00:00'

  - title: A B-52J Bomber Crisis Means a B-21 Raider Bomber Crisis
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/a-b-52j-bomber-crisis-means-a-b-21-raider-bomber-crisis/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – The Air Force plans to keep 76 B-52s flying into
      the 2050s through the B-52J upgrade, but engine, radar, and weapons integration
      delays are pushing schedules right and driving costs up. -A Nunn-McCurdy breach
      raises the stakes: if modernization slips further, long-range strike capacity
      could tighten fast. -The B-52 is […] The post A B-52J Bomber Crisis Means a B-21
      Raider Bomber Crisis appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The Air Force's B-52J upgrade, essential for maintaining long-range
      strike capacity into the 2050s, faces delays and rising costs due to issues with
      engine, radar, and weapons integration, raising concerns about modernization and
      its implications for the B-21 Raider bomber program.
    paragraph_summary: The U.S. Air Force intends to maintain 76 B-52 bombers operational
      into the 2050s with the B-52J upgrade; however, delays in engine, radar, and weapons
      integration are causing schedule setbacks and increasing costs. A Nunn-McCurdy
      breach heightens concerns, as further delays in modernization could significantly
      impact long-range strike capabilities. This situation raises alarms not only for
      the B-52 program but also for the B-21 Raider bomber, indicating a broader crisis
      in the Air Force's long-range strike strategy.
    published: '2025-12-17T19:45:13+00:00'

  - title: We Should Stop Calling the Air Force B-21 Raider a Bomber
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/we-should-stop-calling-the-air-force-b-21-raider-a-bomber/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The B-21 Raider is often framed as the B-2’s replacement,
      but its real value goes far beyond dropping bombs. -Built around open-systems
      architecture and rapid tech insertion, the Raider is designed to evolve as threats
      change and to act as a penetrating sensor and command node inside Joint All-Domain
      Command […] The post We Should Stop Calling the Air Force B-21 Raider a Bomber
      appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The B-21 Raider should not merely be viewed as a replacement
      for the B-2 bomber, as its true significance lies in its advanced open-systems
      architecture and capability to adapt to evolving threats, serving as a critical
      sensor and command node within Joint All-Domain Command.
    paragraph_summary: The B-21 Raider is frequently viewed as a successor to the B-2
      bomber, but its significance extends well beyond traditional bombing roles. Designed
      with an open-systems architecture and the capability for rapid technological updates,
      the Raider is intended to adapt to evolving threats and serve as a penetrating
      sensor and command node within the framework of Joint All-Domain Command. This
      broader functionality suggests that labeling the B-21 solely as a bomber underestimates
      its potential contributions to modern military operations.

      bird strike, which Moscow misinterpreted as evidence that outdated Soviet surface-to-air
      missiles could effectively target modern stealth aircraft.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/why-the-u-s-navy-quit-building-a-mach-7-railgun-with-a-100-mile-range/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – The U.S. Navy once touted the electromagnetic railgun

      gunpowder-free ammo. -After 15 years and more than $500 million, the program was
      shelved in 2021. -Engineering reality killed the dream: barrels that burned out

    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. Navy abandoned its ambitious electromagnetic railgun
      project, which promised high-speed, long-range capabilities, after 15 years and
      over $500 million due to engineering challenges, including rapid barrel wear.
    paragraph_summary: The U.S. Navy's ambitious electromagnetic railgun project, which
      promised high-speed Mach 7 projectiles with a 100-nautical-mile range and cost-effective,
      gunpowder-free ammunition, was ultimately abandoned in 2021 after 15 years and
      over $500 million in investment. The program faced insurmountable engineering
      challenges, including barrel degradation after only a few dozen shots, leading
      to its discontinuation despite initial enthusiasm for its potential as a revolutionary
      naval weapon.

      across Europe, with similar incidents previously reported in Italy and other locations.

      concern over the potential risks involved.

    one_sentence_summary: The B-1B Lancer, originally designed as a Cold War penetrator,
      has become less effective against modern high-threat air defenses due to design
      tradeoffs that eliminated its nuclear capabilities and standoff missiles.
    paragraph_summary: The B-1B Lancer bomber was initially designed to combine the
      speed of the B-58 with the range and payload capacity of the B-52, serving as
      a low-level penetrator during the Cold War and later becoming a key asset in conventional
      operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. However, design compromises, such as the exclusion
      of nuclear weapons and standoff missiles, have rendered the B-1B poorly equipped
      to contend with modern high-threat air defense systems, particularly those of
      Russia, highlighting a fundamental limitation that cannot be rectified.

      navies around the world regarding the evolution of naval warfare and ship design.

      American military and covert presence in the Caribbean. Officially, the move is
      framed around narco-trafficking, pressure on Nicolás Maduro’s illegitimate regime,
      and stemming migrant flows. -Yet Venezuela’s vast underused oil reserves […] The

      airspace "closed" under the pretext of combating narco-trafficking and addressing
      migration issues, but the move is widely interpreted as a strategic maneuver to
      control Venezuela's significant oil reserves amid increasing U.S. military presence
      in the Caribbean.
    paragraph_summary: In late November 2025, President Trump announced the closure
      of Venezuelan airspace, raising concerns in Caracas and among U.S. allies as American
      military and covert operations increased in the Caribbean. While the official
      rationale cites narco-trafficking, pressure on Nicolás Maduro's regime, and controlling
      migrant flows, the article suggests that the underlying motivation may be Venezuela's
      significant but underutilized oil reserves, indicating that the U.S. interest
      in the region is more about oil than drugs.

    paragraph_summary: For ten years, the MiG-25 Foxbat was perceived as a formidable

      high fuel consumption, which contrasted sharply with its fearsome reputation.

    one_sentence_summary: NASA's Hyper-X program successfully demonstrated hydrogen-fueled
      scramjet flight with the X-43A at speeds of Mach 7-10, but the planned Mach 15
      X-43D was ultimately canceled due to shifting budgets and priorities, highlighting
      the need for real flight data in hypersonic conditions for the Air Force.
    paragraph_summary: NASA's Hyper-X program successfully demonstrated hydrogen-fueled
      scramjet flight with the X-43A, achieving speeds of Mach 7 to 10. However, the
      subsequent planned vehicle, the Mach 15 X-43D, was ultimately canceled due to
      shifting budgets, leadership priorities, and organizational changes within the
      agency. The X-43D was intended to collect real flight data under extreme hypersonic
      conditions to mitigate risks for future hypersonic technologies, highlighting
      a missed opportunity for the Air Force in advancing its capabilities in this area.

    one_sentence_summary: The Su-57 Felon, intended to establish Russia's fifth-generation

      country's industrial shortcomings, with production lagging and fewer than 20 operational
      jets.
    paragraph_summary: The Su-57 Felon, intended to serve as the cornerstone of Russia's
      fifth-generation air power and rival the U.S. F-22 and F-35 as well as China's
      J-20, has instead highlighted the country's industrial shortcomings. With fewer
      than 20 serial jets produced and an annual output of only two to four units, the
      fighter's development has been sluggish, and it has yet to receive its long-promised
      Izdeliye-30 engines. This situation raises questions about the aircraft's effectiveness
      as a stealth fighter.

    text: Key Points and Summary – Washington has parked serious naval and air power

      against a country the size of Venezuela would require at least 50,000 U.S. troops,

      Venezuela and indicated that Nicolás Maduro's regime is nearing its end, but a
      full-scale invasion would necessitate a substantial ground force and logistical
      support.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the significant military presence the U.S.
      has established near Venezuela, including naval and air power, and the seizure
      of ships, while indicating that Nicolás Maduro's regime is nearing its end. However,
      it emphasizes that transitioning from this pressure to a full-scale invasion poses
      substantial challenges, as a ground campaign in a country as large as Venezuela

  - title: Saab 37 Viggen Has a Message for the U.S. Air Force F-35 Stealth Fighter
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/saab-37-viggen-has-a-message-for-the-u-s-air-force-f-35-stealth-fighter/
    text: 'Key Points and Article Summary: Sweden’s Saab 37 Viggen was purpose-built
      for a particular Cold War concept: disperse fighters onto highway strips under
      the Bas 60 and later Bas 90 basing systems so the Soviet Union could never wipe
      out the Swedish Air Force in a first strike. -Its single afterburning engine,
      thrust reverser, and […] The post Saab 37 Viggen Has a Message for the U.S. Air
      Force F-35 Stealth Fighter appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The Saab 37 Viggen was designed during the Cold War to ensure
      the Swedish Air Force's survivability against a Soviet first strike by utilizing
      highway strips for deployment, offering lessons for the U.S. Air Force's F-35
      stealth fighter.
    paragraph_summary: The Saab 37 Viggen was designed during the Cold War to enhance
      Sweden's air defense by enabling the deployment of fighters on highway strips,
      thereby preventing the Soviet Union from easily targeting the Swedish Air Force
      in a surprise attack. Its unique features, such as a single afterburning engine
      and thrust reverser, highlight its adaptability and operational strategy. The
      article suggests that the Viggen's design principles could offer valuable insights
      for the U.S. Air Force's F-35 stealth fighter, particularly in terms of survivability
      and operational flexibility in modern warfare.
    published: '2025-12-12T15:21:02+00:00'

      in aerial warfare.

    text: Key Points and Summary – China’s naval strategy around aircraft carriers is
      not contradictory, even if it looks that way. -Beijing fields DF-21D and DF-26
      “carrier killer” missiles and other A2/AD systems to keep U.S. carrier groups
      at risk in its near seas and complicate any intervention over Taiwan or disputed
      waters. -But missiles cannot […] The post China Wants a Fleet of Aircraft Carriers
      (And To Destroy Aircraft Carriers) appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: China's naval strategy aims to develop a fleet of aircraft
      carriers while simultaneously deploying anti-access/area denial (A2/AD) systems
      and "carrier killer" missiles to deter U.S. carrier groups and complicate military
      interventions in its near seas.
    paragraph_summary: China's naval strategy regarding aircraft carriers may seem contradictory,
      as it aims to both develop a fleet of carriers and deploy advanced anti-access/area
      denial (A2/AD) systems, such as the DF-21D and DF-26 "carrier killer" missiles,
      to threaten U.S. carrier groups in its near seas. This dual approach is designed
      to deter U.S. intervention in regional conflicts, particularly over Taiwan and
      disputed waters. While these missiles enhance China's defensive capabilities,
      they also highlight the complexities of modern naval warfare, where the presence
      of aircraft carriers is still deemed essential for power projection.

      aircraft.

  - title: China’s Mach 5 DF-17 Hypersonic Missile Has a Message for the U.S. Navy
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/chinas-mach-5-df-17-hypersonic-missile-has-a-message-for-the-u-s-navy/
    text: Key Points and Summary – China’s DF-17 hypersonic missile sits at the heart
      of Beijing’s “Assassin’s Mace” strategy to keep U.S. carrier strike groups at
      bay in the Indo-Pacific. -Mated to the DF-ZF hypersonic glide vehicle, the solid-fueled
      DF-17 can maneuver at Mach 5–10, skim the atmosphere, and threaten ships or land
      targets out past […] The post China’s Mach 5 DF-17 Hypersonic Missile Has a Message
      for the U.S. Navy appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: China's DF-17 hypersonic missile, part of its "Assassin's
      Mace" strategy, is designed to deter U.S. carrier strike groups in the Indo-Pacific
      by maneuvering at speeds of Mach 5–10 and targeting both ships and land-based
      assets.
    paragraph_summary: China's DF-17 hypersonic missile is a crucial component of Beijing's
      "Assassin’s Mace" strategy aimed at deterring U.S. carrier strike groups in the
      Indo-Pacific region. This missile, equipped with the DF-ZF hypersonic glide vehicle,
      boasts the capability to maneuver at speeds between Mach 5 and 10, allowing it
      to skim the atmosphere and pose a significant threat to both maritime and land
      targets at extended ranges. The development of the DF-17 underscores China's efforts
      to enhance its military capabilities and challenge U.S. naval dominance in the
      area.

    one_sentence_summary: The YF-118G "Bird of Prey," developed by McDonnell Douglas/Boeing
      in the 1990s, was a low-cost stealth fighter designed primarily as a testbed for
      advancing stealth technology and manufacturing techniques rather than for combat
      or public display.
    paragraph_summary: The YF-118G "Bird of Prey," developed by McDonnell Douglas/Boeing
      in the 1990s, was designed not for aerial combat or public displays but as a cost-effective,
      secretive testbed to advance stealth technology, infrared signature reduction,
      and innovative manufacturing methods. Featuring a blended-wing-body and a tailless
      design, the aircraft played a crucial role in maturing stealth capabilities, offering
      valuable insights for the Air Force's future developments in stealth fighters.

      fighter jet never built. -A skipped designation between the F/A-18 and F-20, Cold

      some foreign militaries—that a secret F-19 stealth fighter existed. -Model-maker

      with advanced military technology, serving as a cautionary tale for the U.S. Air
      Force.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the F-19, a legendary fighter jet that
      never actually existed, which became a symbol of Cold War intrigue during the
      1980s. Its skipped designation between the F/A-18 and F-20, along with rumors
      of radar-evading "black projects," fueled public and military speculation about
      its existence. Model-maker Revell capitalized on this myth, further embedding
      the F-19 in popular culture. The piece suggests that the story of the F-19 carries
      a relevant message for the U.S. Air Force today, likely highlighting the importance
      of transparency and communication in military advancements.

    text: Key Points and Summary – Germany’s so-called “pocket battleships” — Deutschland,
      Admiral Scheer, and Admiral Graf Spee — were Hitler’s workaround to interwar naval
      limits, combining diesel propulsion, 11-inch guns, and long range in relatively
      light hulls. -Optimized to terrorize merchant shipping, they found early success
      in commerce raiding but proved too lightly armored and […] The post Germany’s
      ‘Pocket’ Battleships Have a Message for Every Navy on Earth appeared first on
      19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: Germany's "pocket battleships," including the Deutschland,
      Admiral Scheer, and Admiral Graf Spee, were designed to circumvent interwar naval
      restrictions with their unique combination of diesel engines, 11-inch guns, and
      long range, effectively targeting merchant shipping despite their vulnerabilities
      in armor.
    paragraph_summary: Germany's "pocket battleships"—the Deutschland, Admiral Scheer,
      and Admiral Graf Spee—were designed by Hitler as a means to circumvent the naval
      restrictions imposed after World War I. These ships featured diesel propulsion,
      11-inch guns, and long-range capabilities within a relatively lightweight framework,
      making them effective for commerce raiding against merchant shipping. However,
      their success was limited by their inadequate armor, highlighting important lessons
      for modern navies regarding the balance between firepower, armor, and operational
      strategy.

  - title: 'J-10 vs. F-16: The Secret Israeli DNA in China’s ‘Vigorous Dragon’ Fighter'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/j-10-vs-f-16-the-secret-israeli-dna-in-chinas-vigorous-dragon-fighter/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – China’s J-10 “Vigorous Dragon” was billed as Beijing’s
      homegrown answer to the F-16, but its real origins are far more complicated. -In
      the 1990s, as Israel sought export markets for its canceled Lavi fighter, key
      technologies in avionics, flight controls, composites, missiles, and sensors quietly
      flowed to China’s Chengdu Aircraft […] The post J-10 vs. F-16: The Secret Israeli
      DNA in China’s ‘Vigorous Dragon’ Fighter appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: China's J-10 fighter, marketed as a domestic alternative to
      the F-16, actually incorporates significant Israeli technology from the 1990s,
      stemming from the canceled Lavi fighter program.
    paragraph_summary: China's J-10 fighter, known as the "Vigorous Dragon," was initially
      presented as a domestic alternative to the F-16, but its development is rooted
      in a complex history involving foreign technology transfers. In the 1990s, Israel,
      looking to market its canceled Lavi fighter, inadvertently provided China’s Chengdu
      Aircraft with crucial technologies related to avionics, flight controls, composites,
      missiles, and sensors. This collaboration highlights the intricate and often secretive
      connections between nations in the aerospace sector, revealing the J-10's reliance
      on Israeli innovations despite its portrayal as a purely Chinese creation.
    published: '2025-12-08T16:45:07+00:00'

      Force collaborated on the development of the L-301, also known as the X-24C, a

      a scramjet engine after an initial rocket boost. Drawing on insights from the
      X-15 program and lifting-body research, the L-301 was intended to be air-launched
      from a B-52 bomber, highlighting the ambitious nature of hypersonic flight technology
      during that era and its implications for modern military capabilities.

      is advancing submarine technology with the new Blekinge-class, or A26, which is
      larger and more capable than the Gotland-class while still utilizing the Stirling
      engine for air-independent propulsion. This evolution in submarine design underscores
      the ongoing significance of stealth and advanced capabilities in modern naval
      warfare.

      fighter designed to integrate seamlessly with allied networks. In contrast, the
      NGAD initiative is characterized by its high costs and sophisticated technology,

      GCAP fighter could potentially revolutionize stealth capabilities in air combat.

  - title: Donald Trump Revives the Monroe Doctrine – and Gets It Dangerously Wrong
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/donald-trump-revives-the-monroe-doctrine-and-gets-it-dangerously-wrong/
    text: Key Points and Summary – Donald Trump’s anniversary proclamation for the Monroe
      Doctrine adds a “Trump Corollary,” vowing that only Americans will shape their
      hemisphere’s destiny. -Dr. Michael Rubin argues this “Donroe Doctrine” misunderstands
      Monroe’s intent and today’s reality. -Monroe paired Western-hemisphere vigilance
      with noninterference elsewhere. -Trump, by contrast, flirts with 21st-century
      isolationism just as […] The post Donald Trump Revives the Monroe Doctrine – and
      Gets It Dangerously Wrong appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: Donald Trump's anniversary proclamation for the Monroe Doctrine
      introduces a "Trump Corollary" that asserts American dominance in shaping the
      hemisphere's future, but Dr. Michael Rubin argues this misinterprets Monroe's
      original intent of vigilance coupled with noninterference and risks promoting
      modern isolationism.
    paragraph_summary: In a recent proclamation commemorating the Monroe Doctrine, Donald
      Trump introduced a "Trump Corollary," asserting that only Americans should determine
      the future of the Western Hemisphere. Dr. Michael Rubin critiques this interpretation,
      suggesting that it misrepresents the original intent of the Monroe Doctrine, which
      balanced vigilance in the Western Hemisphere with a policy of noninterference
      in other regions. Rubin warns that Trump's approach leans towards a form of 21st-century
      isolationism, diverging from the historical principles established by Monroe.
    published: '2025-12-05T12:50:01+00:00'

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/mini-chernobyl-the-secret-russian-navy-nuclear-submarine-meltdown-moscow-tried-to-bury/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Months before Chernobyl, the Soviet Navy suffered
      a major nuclear disaster when the Echo-II submarine K-431 blew its reactor during
      “routine” refueling in Chazhma Bay near Vladivostok. -A mishandled reactor lid
      triggered a prompt criticality, killing nearly a dozen sailors and irradiating
      hundreds more as radioactive debris showered nearby ships […] The post Mini Chernobyl:
      The Secret Russian Navy Nuclear Submarine Meltdown Moscow Tried to Bury appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: Months before the Chernobyl disaster, the Soviet Navy's Echo-II
      submarine K-431 experienced a catastrophic reactor meltdown during routine refueling
      in Chazhma Bay, resulting in the deaths of nearly a dozen sailors and widespread
      radiation exposure to hundreds more.
    paragraph_summary: Months prior to the Chernobyl disaster, the Soviet Navy experienced
      a significant nuclear incident when the Echo-II submarine K-431's reactor exploded
      during routine refueling in Chazhma Bay, near Vladivostok. A mishandled reactor
      lid led to a prompt criticality, resulting in the deaths of nearly a dozen sailors
      and exposing hundreds more to radiation as radioactive debris fell onto nearby
      vessels. This event, often referred to as a "mini Chernobyl," was largely concealed
      by the Soviet authorities.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/why-the-navys-sixth-gen-f-a-xx-fighter-must-be-a-2000-mile-pacific-sniper/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The Pacific theater’s “tyranny of distance” will
      define whether the Navy’s sixth-generation F/A-XX succeeds or fails. -With Chinese
      DF-26 “carrier-killer” missiles reaching roughly 2,000 miles, carriers may be
      forced to operate far from key targets, demanding a fighter with nearly double
      the F-35C’s range, real on-station dwell time, and deep-strike […] The post Why
      the Navy’s Sixth-Gen F/A-XX Fighter Must Be a 2,000-Mile Pacific ‘Sniper’ appeared
      first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The success of the Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter
      hinges on its ability to operate effectively at long ranges in the Pacific theater,
      particularly in response to threats like China's DF-26 missiles, necessitating
      a range nearly double that of the F-35C.
    paragraph_summary: The success of the Navy's sixth-generation F/A-XX fighter in
      the Pacific theater hinges on its ability to overcome the "tyranny of distance,"
      particularly in light of China's DF-26 "carrier-killer" missiles that can strike
      targets up to 2,000 miles away. This necessitates a fighter with nearly double
      the range of the F-35C, as well as capabilities for real on-station dwell time
      and deep-strike missions. The article emphasizes that to effectively operate in
      this challenging environment, the F/A-XX must function as a long-range "sniper"
      to ensure the safety and effectiveness of naval operations.
    published: '2025-12-04T17:41:00+00:00'

    text: Key Points and Summary – On January 14, 1969, the nuclear-powered carrier

      an F-4, triggering a chain reaction of explosions, ruptured fuel tanks, and burning
      JP-5 pouring through the deck. […] The post A Single Rocket Turned a Nuclear Navy
      Aircraft Carrier Into a ‘Fireball Inferno’ appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: On January 14, 1969, the USS Enterprise experienced a catastrophic
      flight deck fire near Hawaii, initiated by hot exhaust igniting a Zuni rocket,
      which led to a series of explosions and widespread flames.
    paragraph_summary: On January 14, 1969, the USS Enterprise, a nuclear-powered aircraft
      carrier, experienced a catastrophic fire on its flight deck while getting ready
      for combat operations near Hawaii. The incident began when hot exhaust from a
      "huffer" ignited a Zuni rocket on an F-4 Phantom jet, leading to a series of explosions,
      ruptured fuel tanks, and burning JP-5 fuel cascading across the deck, resulting
      in a devastating inferno.

      with meeting Canadian security standards ultimately led to the collapse of its
      bid.

      by regional security concerns and recent developments in U.S.-South Korea defense
      agreements.

      nuclear power in the context of military capabilities, particularly regarding
      the potential replacement of its diesel submarines with nuclear-powered ones.
      This shift in perspective has been influenced by recent developments, including
      a U.S.–South Korea nuclear submarine agreement, China's expanding naval presence,
      and increased tensions surrounding Taiwan. As Japan evaluates its postwar nuclear
      policies, the debate over adopting nuclear submarines marks a significant change
      in its defense strategy, reflecting the evolving security landscape in the region.

  - title: Canada Has a Message for the F/A-18 Super Hornet Fighter
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/canada-has-a-message-for-the-f-a-18-super-hornet-fighter/
    text: Key Points and Summary – Canada’s plan to replace its aging CF-18 fleet turned
      into a political and industrial drama that ultimately doomed Boeing’s F/A-18 Super
      Hornet. -Ottawa dropped the Super Hornet from its 88-jet competition after Boeing
      launched a trade case against Canadian aerospace champion Bombardier, prompting
      new rules penalizing firms seen as harming […] The post Canada Has a Message for
      the F/A-18 Super Hornet Fighter appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: Canada's decision to exclude Boeing's F/A-18 Super Hornet
      from its fighter jet competition stemmed from a political fallout following Boeing's
      trade dispute with Bombardier, leading to new rules that penalized companies perceived
      as detrimental to Canadian industry.
    paragraph_summary: Canada's decision to replace its aging CF-18 fleet has led to
      significant political and industrial tensions, ultimately resulting in the exclusion
      of Boeing's F/A-18 Super Hornet from the competition for 88 new jets. This decision
      followed Boeing's trade case against Canadian aerospace company Bombardier, which
      prompted Canada to implement new rules that penalize companies perceived as undermining
      local industries. The situation highlights the complexities and repercussions
      of international trade disputes on defense procurement processes.
    published: '2025-12-04T15:14:11+00:00'

    text: 'Key Points and Summary – After losing the Air Force’s Next Generation Air

      to achieve significant sixth-generation capabilities at a lower cost, positioning
      it as a potential alternative for the U.S. Air Force.
    paragraph_summary: After losing the Air Force's Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD)
      competition to Boeing's F-47, Lockheed Martin is pivoting to an ambitious alternative
      strategy, proposing a high-performance version of the F-35, dubbed the "Ferrari"
      F-35. CEO Jim Taiclet claims that this upgraded model can achieve approximately
      80% of sixth-generation capabilities at half the cost by integrating advanced
      NGAD technologies into the existing F-35 airframe. This approach positions the
      F-35 as a potential frontrunner for the future of U.S. Air Force fighter aircraft.

    paragraph_summary: After losing the Air Force's Next Generation Air Dominance (NGAD)
      competition to Boeing's F-47, Lockheed Martin is pivoting to an ambitious alternative
      strategy, proposing a high-performance version of the F-35, dubbed the "Ferrari"
      F-35. CEO Jim Taiclet claims that this upgraded model can achieve approximately
      80% of sixth-generation capabilities at half the cost by integrating advanced
      NGAD technologies into the existing F-35 airframe. This approach positions the
      F-35 as a potential frontrunner for the future of U.S. Air Force fighter aircraft.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-f-22-raptor-fighter-mistake-that-has-generals-shaking-their-heads/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The F-22 Raptor is widely regarded as the world’s
      premier air-superiority fighter, yet the U.S. will never build more of them. -Production
      was capped at 187 jets after then–Defense Secretary Bob Gates killed the program
      in 2009 to free up funding for the B-21 bomber and counterinsurgency priorities,
      assuming great […] The post The F-22 Raptor Fighter Mistake That Has Generals
      Shaking Their Heads appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The U.S. has capped F-22 Raptor production at 187 jets due
      to budget reallocations, despite its status as the world's top air-superiority
      fighter, leaving military leaders concerned about the decision.
    paragraph_summary: The F-22 Raptor, considered the world's leading air-superiority
      fighter, will not see any further production beyond the 187 jets already built,
      a decision made by former Defense Secretary Bob Gates in 2009 to allocate resources
      towards the B-21 bomber and counterinsurgency efforts. This decision has led to
      frustration among military leaders, who view it as a significant oversight given
      the aircraft's unmatched capabilities in air combat.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/russias-mig-35-fighter-fiasco/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The MiG-35 was sold as Russia’s affordable, export-ready
      answer to the F-16 and Gripen—a “4++” bridge between aging MiG-29s and modern
      air combat. -In reality, it never delivered. -The promised AESA radar and advanced
      engines failed to materialize in operational jets, leaving a warmed-over MiG-29
      in a fifth-generation world. -Moscow […] The post Russia’s MiG-35 Fighter Fiasco
      appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The MiG-35, marketed as Russia's cost-effective alternative
      to the F-16 and Gripen, ultimately fell short of expectations due to the absence
      of promised advanced technology, resulting in a fighter that resembles an outdated
      MiG-29 in a modern combat landscape.
    paragraph_summary: The MiG-35 was marketed by Russia as an affordable, export-ready
      alternative to the F-16 and Gripen, positioned as a "4++" fighter to bridge the
      gap between outdated MiG-29s and modern air combat capabilities. However, it has
      not lived up to expectations, as the anticipated advanced features like AESA radar
      and modern engines were not included in the operational jets, resulting in a fighter
      that essentially resembles an upgraded MiG-29 rather than a competitive option
      in the fifth-generation landscape.

    text: Key Points and Summary – Russia’s Su-57 Felon was billed as a true fifth-generation
      rival to the F-22, F-35, and China’s J-20. -Instead, it has become a low-volume,
      high-hype program. -Chronic production bottlenecks, sanctions, engine delays,
      and questionable stealth features mean fewer than 20 serial jets likely exist,
      all flying with a stopgap fourth-generation powerplant. […] The post Russia’s
      Su-57 Felon Stealth Fighter Might Not Even Be a Stealth Fighter appeared first
      on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: Russia's Su-57 Felon, initially promoted as a fifth-generation
      stealth fighter to rival the F-22, F-35, and China's J-20, has faced significant
      production challenges and limitations, resulting in fewer than 20 operational
      jets that rely on outdated technology.
    paragraph_summary: Russia's Su-57 Felon was initially promoted as a formidable fifth-generation
      stealth fighter to compete with the F-22, F-35, and China's J-20. However, it
      has turned into a low-volume, high-hype program plagued by production bottlenecks,
      sanctions, engine delays, and doubts about its stealth capabilities. As a result,
      it is estimated that fewer than 20 operational jets exist, all currently utilizing
      a temporary fourth-generation engine instead of the intended advanced powerplant.

      American naval strength, featuring five massive ships that displaced over 60,000

      mightiest enemy fire, such as that from Japan's Yamato. Authorized in 1940, these
      battleships prioritized firepower and protection over the speed of the Iowa-class,
      but ultimately, they were never completed or deployed.

      just one confirmed kill—against a Chinese spy balloon. -With only 187 airframes
      ever built, production lines shut down, a sky-high cost per flight hour, and mission-capable
      rates hovering around […] The post Is the Air Force Afraid to Send the F-22 Raptor

    one_sentence_summary: The F-22 Raptor, designed as America's premier air superiority
      fighter, has seen limited combat success with only one confirmed kill and faces
      challenges such as high operational costs and low mission-capable rates, raising
      questions about the Air Force's willingness to deploy it in conflict.

      such as high operational costs and low mission-capable rates, raising questions
      about the Air Force's willingness to deploy it in combat situations.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/334000000-per-plane-the-f-22-raptor-is-the-most-expensive-fighter-ever/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – The F-22 Raptor was supposed to be America’s premier
      air dominance fighter, but a 2009 decision to cap production at 187 jets turned
      it into a boutique fleet with boutique costs. -Program spending topped $67 billion,
      pushing per-aircraft cost north of $300 million, while flying each Raptor now
      runs over […] The post $334,000,000 Per Plane: The F-22 Raptor Is the Most Expensive
      Fighter Ever appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The F-22 Raptor, initially intended as America's leading air
      dominance fighter, became a costly boutique fleet due to a 2009 production cap,
      resulting in a total program cost exceeding $67 billion and a staggering per-aircraft
      expense of over $300 million.
    paragraph_summary: The F-22 Raptor, initially designed to be the United States'
      leading air dominance fighter, has become an expensive and limited fleet due to
      a 2009 decision to cap production at 187 jets. This decision has resulted in program
      costs exceeding $67 billion, leading to a staggering per-aircraft cost of over
      $300 million. Consequently, the operational cost of flying each Raptor now exceeds
      $334,000, making it the most expensive fighter jet in history.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/12/the-f-a-xx-6th-generation-stealth-fighter-has-a-message-for-the-navy/

      of propulsion during deep-dive trials. This incident highlighted the need for
      improved safety measures, ultimately shaping the protocols that protect sailors
      today.

      and quieter operations.

      Japan's leading diesel-electric attack submarines, notable for their groundbreaking
      use of Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) and lithium-ion battery technology. The

      to utilize lithium-ion batteries, which enhance submerged endurance and enable
      quieter operations compared to conventional lead-acid batteries. This innovative
      design allows the Sōryū-class submarines to remain submerged for extended periods,
      marking a significant advancement in submarine technology.

    one_sentence_summary: The XB-70 Valkyrie, a Mach 3 bomber developed by the U.S.

      due to advancements in missile technology and changing military needs by the time
      it first flew in 1964.
    paragraph_summary: The XB-70 Valkyrie was a groundbreaking U.S. Air Force bomber
      developed in the 1950s, designed to fly at Mach 3 and reach altitudes of 70,000
      feet, aiming to evade Soviet air defenses and replace the B-52 and B-58 bombers.
      Although it took its first flight in 1964, advancements in Soviet surface-to-air
      missile technology and intercontinental ballistic missiles had already begun to
      alter the strategic landscape, raising questions about the relevance of the XB-70's
      design. The article suggests that the lessons learned from the XB-70's development
      and operational challenges could offer valuable insights for the Air Force in
      addressing modern aerial threats.

    text: 'Key Takeaways – The F-22 Raptor delivered exactly what the Air Force wanted

      to replace the F-15 in the hundreds. Instead, post–Cold War complacency, soaring

      ‘Nightmare’ It Can’t Ever Fly Away From appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The F-22 Raptor successfully met the Air Force's performance
      expectations but failed to achieve the intended production scale due to post-Cold
      War complacency and rising costs.
    paragraph_summary: The F-22 Raptor successfully met the Air Force's expectations
      for stealth, supercruise capabilities, impressive maneuverability, and advanced
      sensors, but it ultimately fell short in terms of production scale. Originally
      intended to replace the F-15 in large numbers as part of the Cold War-era Advanced
      Tactical Fighter (ATF) program, the Raptor's production was hindered by post-Cold
      War complacency, rising unit costs, and changing military priorities, resulting
      in a limited fleet that poses ongoing challenges for the Air Force.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/11/we-left-a-manhole-open-how-a-new-navy-nuclear-submarine-sank-while-docked/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – In 1969, the brand-new nuclear attack submarine
      USS Guitarro famously “sank” pierside at Mare Island after a stunning series of
      blunders. -Workers removed a bolted manhole cover and cofferdam in the bow sonar
      dome to swap out faulty transducers—and never put them back. -Weeks later, simultaneous
      trimming and calibration tests […] The post ‘We Left A Manhole Open’: How A New
      Navy Nuclear Submarine Sank While Docked appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: In 1969, the USS Guitarro, a newly commissioned nuclear submarine,
      sank at Mare Island due to a series of mistakes, including the failure to replace
      a manhole cover and cofferdam after maintenance work.
    paragraph_summary: In 1969, the USS Guitarro, a newly commissioned nuclear attack
      submarine, infamously sank while docked at Mare Island due to a series of critical
      mistakes. Workers had removed a bolted manhole cover and cofferdam from the bow
      sonar dome to replace faulty transducers but failed to reinstall them. This oversight,
      combined with simultaneous trimming and calibration tests, led to the submarine
      taking on water and ultimately sinking at the pier.

    paragraph_summary: In the 1970s, the U.S. Navy contemplated the construction of
      a class of medium aircraft carriers, known as CVVs, weighing between 50,000 and
      60,000 tons, to enhance its aviation capabilities during the Vietnam War and the
      Cold War. These conventionally powered carriers were designed to be more cost-effective
      and quicker to build than the larger Nimitz-class supercarriers, aiming to supplement
      the aging Midway-class ships and bolster naval air power. However, the CVV project
      ultimately did not come to fruition.

      power system. The DDG(X) is specifically engineered to counter threats posed by
      missiles, drones, and lasers, signaling a strategic response to China's military
      capabilities.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/11/the-navy-worried-russias-admiral-kuznetsov-aircraft-carrier-might-sink/
    text: Key Points and Summary – Admiral Kuznetsov was never a normal carrier. Born

      it sailed with balky mazut engines, thick black smoke, and chronic breakdowns
      that made it the butt of NATO jokes. -Yet Moscow kept it alive for decades after
      the Soviet collapse, […] The post The Navy Worried Russia’s Admiral Kuznetsov
      Aircraft Carrier Might Sink appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The Admiral Kuznetsov, originally designed as a heavy aircraft-carrying
      cruiser to circumvent the Montreux Convention, has faced numerous operational
      issues and mockery from NATO, yet Russia has maintained it for decades despite
      its chronic breakdowns and unreliable engines.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the Admiral Kuznetsov, a Russian aircraft
      carrier originally designed as a "heavy aircraft-carrying cruiser" to circumvent
      the Montreux Convention. Despite its problematic mazut engines, which produced
      thick black smoke and frequent breakdowns, the ship remained operational for decades
      following the Soviet Union's collapse, often becoming a target of ridicule among
      NATO forces. The piece highlights ongoing concerns within the Navy regarding the
      vessel's seaworthiness, with fears that it might sink due to its long history
      of mechanical issues.

    one_sentence_summary: Russia's Tu-160 "Blackjack," the world's largest and fastest

      component of Moscow's nuclear strategy, especially amidst delays in the development
      of the stealthy PAK DA.
    paragraph_summary: Russia's Tu-160 "Blackjack" bomber, the largest and fastest in
      the world, continues to play a crucial role in Moscow's nuclear strategy as part
      of its triad. With the development of the stealthy PAK DA facing significant delays,
      Russia is modernizing 16 existing Tu-160 airframes and resuming production of
      the Tu-160M2 variant, which will feature upgraded engines, avionics, and long-range
      cruise missiles that have been utilized in conflicts such as in Syria. This modernization
      effort sends a clear message to the U.S. Air Force regarding Russia's commitment
      to maintaining and enhancing its strategic bomber capabilities.

      bombing capabilities by sacrificing some agility for increased range, payload,
      and hardpoints, highlighting a potential shift in the U.S. Air Force's strategic

    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the FB-22 Strike Raptor, a proposed variant

      enhance the aircraft's capabilities as a stealthy medium bomber. This two-seat
      derivative would have sacrificed some agility for increased range and payload,
      featuring 27 hardpoints for carrying munitions. The FB-22's concept highlights
      the need for the U.S. Air Force to consider versatile aircraft that can fulfill
      both air dominance and strike roles, emphasizing the strategic importance of adapting
      existing technologies to meet evolving military requirements.

      to the submarine but only minor harm to the aircraft carrier, which U.S. officers
      attributed to poor Soviet seamanship.
    paragraph_summary: In 1984, the Soviet Victor-class submarine K-314 collided with
      the USS Kitty Hawk during nighttime exercises in the Sea of Japan, resulting in
      significant damage to the submarine while the aircraft carrier sustained only

      nuclear capabilities. The event underscored the tense military dynamics of the
      Cold War era.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/11/why-the-navy-never-built-deep-diving-titanium-submarines-like-russia/
    text: Key Points and Summary – The US Navy has taken a pragmatic approach to titanium,
      using it sparingly in high-stress components rather than building whole hulls
      from the exotic metal. -Titanium’s strength, corrosion resistance and low magnetic
      signature made it attractive for Soviet designers, who built titanium-hulled boats
      like the Papa and Sierra classes and […] The post Why the Navy Never Built ‘Deep
      Diving’ Titanium Submarines Like Russia appeared first on 19FortyFive .
    one_sentence_summary: The US Navy opts for a practical use of titanium in high-stress
      components rather than constructing entire submarines from the metal, contrasting
      with Soviet designs that utilized titanium hulls for their submarines.
    paragraph_summary: The US Navy has opted for a practical use of titanium, employing
      it selectively in high-stress components rather than constructing entire hulls
      from the metal, unlike the Soviet Union, which utilized titanium extensively for
      submarines such as the Papa and Sierra classes due to its strength, corrosion
      resistance, and low magnetic signature. This strategic choice reflects the Navy's
      focus on efficiency and effectiveness in submarine design, steering away from
      the deep-diving titanium submarines that Russia pursued.

      underlying differences could significantly influence the outcome in a hypothetical
      combat scenario between the two fighters.

    text: 'Key Points and Summary – Post–Cold War cuts turned four Ohio-class boomers
      into fearsome SSGNs, each packing 154 Tomahawk cruise missiles in repurposed Trident
      tubes. -Together with Ticonderoga-class cruisers, they provide 2,080 vertical-launch
      cells—America’s real floating missile magazines. -But all four SSGNs and every
      Tico are slated for retirement by 2027, raising fears of a […] The post 2080 Missiles

      on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The retirement of four Ohio-class SSGNs and Ticonderoga-class
      cruisers by 2027 poses a significant challenge for the U.S. Navy, as these vessels
      currently serve as crucial platforms for launching Tomahawk missiles.
    paragraph_summary: The article discusses the transformation of four Ohio-class submarines
      into SSGNs (guided missile submarines) after post-Cold War cuts, allowing each
      to carry 154 Tomahawk cruise missiles in repurposed Trident tubes. Together with
      Ticonderoga-class cruisers, these vessels create a formidable arsenal with 2,080
      vertical-launch cells, effectively serving as America's floating missile magazines.
      However, concerns are rising as all four SSGNs and every Ticonderoga-class cruiser
      are scheduled for retirement by 2027, which could significantly impact the U.S.
      Navy's missile capabilities.

      of modern stealth aircraft, highlighting the evolution of military aviation technology.

    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/11/the-b-21-raider-might-have-a-battleship-problem/
    text: Article Summary – Talk of drones and AI “revolutionizing” warfare repeats
      the same RMA hype of the 1990s. Technologies like the B-21 Raider, unmanned systems,
      and AI are powerful, but they are evolutionary advances, not game-changers that
      alter war’s fundamental character. -The B-21 still performs classic missions—deterrence,
      deep strike, nuclear and conventional signaling—only with better […] The post
      The B-21 Raider Might Have a ‘Battleship’ Problem appeared first on 19FortyFive
      .
    one_sentence_summary: The article argues that while technologies like the B-21 Raider
      and AI are significant advancements in warfare, they represent evolutionary rather
      than revolutionary changes, continuing to fulfill traditional military roles rather
      than fundamentally altering the nature of war.
    paragraph_summary: The article argues that the current excitement surrounding drones
      and AI in warfare mirrors the hype of the 1990s regarding Revolutionary Military
      Affairs (RMA). While technologies like the B-21 Raider and unmanned systems represent
      significant advancements, they do not fundamentally change the nature of warfare;
      rather, they enhance traditional military missions such as deterrence and deep
      strikes. The B-21, despite its advanced capabilities, still fulfills classic roles,
      suggesting that these innovations are evolutionary rather than revolutionary,
      akin to the historical challenges faced by battleships in adapting to new forms
      of warfare.
    published: '2025-11-25T12:17:51+00:00'

    paragraph_summary: The F-105 Thunderchief, affectionately known as the "Thud," was
      initially designed as a supersonic nuclear strike aircraft but evolved into the
      U.S. Air Force's main fighter-bomber during the Vietnam War. Manufactured by Republic
      Aviation, this powerful single-engine jet was capable of carrying a bomb load
      heavier than that of World War II heavy bombers while achieving speeds of Mach
      2. Despite its impressive capabilities, pilots often referred to the F-105 as
      a "flying coffin" due to its high casualty rates in combat, yet it remained a
      beloved aircraft among those who flew it.

      a precarious and uncertain situation.

  - title: 'No Place to Hide: The End of Submarine Stealth?'
    url: https://www.19fortyfive.com/2025/11/no-place-to-hide-the-end-of-submarine-stealth/
    text: 'Key Points and Summary – U.S. submarines still own the acoustic fight, but
      a wave of non-acoustic sensors is narrowing the gap. -A Naval Submarine League
      analysis spotlights magnetic anomaly detection (MAD), bioluminescent “boundary
      layer” wakes, surface and internal wave signatures, thermal trails seen by IR,
      and blue-green laser lidar that can ping through seawater. […] The post No Place
      to Hide: The End of Submarine Stealth? appeared first on 19FortyFive .'
    one_sentence_summary: The article discusses how while U.S. submarines maintain superiority
      in acoustic detection, emerging non-acoustic sensors like magnetic anomaly detection
      and thermal imaging are increasingly challenging their stealth capabilities.
    paragraph_summary: A recent analysis by the Naval Submarine League highlights that
      while U.S. submarines maintain superiority in acoustic detection, emerging non-acoustic
      sensors are increasingly challenging their stealth capabilities. Technologies
      such as magnetic anomaly detection (MAD), bioluminescent wakes, surface and internal
      wave signatures, infrared thermal trails, and blue-green laser lidar are becoming
      more effective at detecting submarines, potentially diminishing their ability
      to operate undetected. This shift raises concerns about the future of submarine
      stealth in naval warfare.
    published: '2025-11-10T20:47:29+00:00'
